66: And now we have established the Halacha like R. Shimon that we are not concerned for sealing  - a pierced hole which can be done without effort, because it can be discerned, and additionally entirely opening the lid, that R. Shimon is concerned for, we do not establish [the halacha] like him, because that type of forging involves effort, and we have established in (Chapter) Eiyn Mamidim (earlier daf 31a) the halacha is in accordance with R. Eliezer whom is not concerned for the forgery of [even] a single seal. For why did we not question him from [our case here of] sealed barrels in the hand of gentiles {where there is concern even according to R Shimon of possible forgery}.

Because of the slot - Extremely narrow hole in the bung of the barrel, to enable the wine vapours to escape. There is a concern that perhaps it may have been somewhat bored and he [the gentile] will have tasted of the wine.
